title: Durable journal, reconciliation and resume (RJ-01 to RJ-03)
objective: Make every state-changing step orceld dispatches recoverable without repeating a side effect. The download intent journal SG-000108 qualified becomes a shared kernel journal crate (RJ-01); every mutating dispatch of the RJ-02 providers (fs write, edit, move and remove; git mutations including git push; desktop actions; clipboard write; process spawn; and the SG-000126 report commit) records an intent before it runs and settles it after, and after a lost reply, crash or restart the provider's own reconciliation probe decides settled, abandoned or unknown, never re-dispatching (RJ-02); a reconnecting local client can read a bounded, factual summary of what finished, what is unknown and what each unknown step needs verified (RJ-03). Report task records (SG-000126) become durable across a restart through the same journal. This activation authorizes none of these by itself.

include: Activate the SG-000120 contract only. RJ-01, RJ-02 and RJ-03 each need their own exact-head qualified implementation PR, and each needs a fresh-context security judge.

RJ-01, journal crate: move the generic parts of the SG-000108 intent journal (crates/orceld/src/live_browser.rs: the line append with torn-tail sealing and the line reader) into crates/orcel-journal: a one-writer journal with states pending -> dispatched -> settled | abandoned | unknown -> reconciled; bounded line and file size; fsync on every append and a parent directory sync on Unix. Reading keeps SG-000108's rule exactly: a torn line (a strict prefix whose JSON ends early, sealed by a later append or at the tail, with zero bytes dropped) is skipped and reported as a typed warning; every other unreadable line, unknown event or wrong schema fails closed. A second writer is refused (fs4 lock, already a workspace dependency). intents.jsonl stays byte-compatible, the SG-000108 download writer emits only its four existing events (pending, settled, abandoned, reconciled), and every SG-000108 suite passes unchanged. The crate names neither of SG-000108's test-only or development-only browser features (crates/orcel-lifecycle/tests/release_blocker_sweep.rs), joins neither of their sweep allowlists and carries no browser capability, so it may link into release builds; DownloadIntent, reconcile_destination and host liveness stay in live_browser.rs under their existing cfg.

RJ-02, journal and reconcile every mutating dispatch of these providers: fs write, edit, move and remove; git mutations including git push; desktop actions; clipboard write; process spawn; and the SG-000126 report commit. Each records an intent bound to the approval digest before dispatch and settles it after. Reconciliation is per provider and local: fs and report compare the destination's existence and content hash with the approved digest; git probes local ref and index state, and git push reconciles as unknown unless local evidence settles it (no network probe); desktop actions stay unknown: a re-observation may be shown to the user but never marks the step settled; process records pid and start generation and probes the exit record. A retry is any dispatch under the same intent id or approval digest, and none happens: re-running a step whose outcome is unknown needs a fresh approval and a fresh intent, and every later mutating step of the same task is refused until then.

RJ-02, durable report tasks: SG-000126 task records survive an orceld restart through the journal, without changing the create-only and verifier rules, so task.list and task.get keep reporting them, and a report commit interrupted after approval is reconciled against the destination instead of written again.

RJ-03, resume summary: classify journal entries into completed and interrupted-unknown with input fingerprints (a keyed hash under orceld's state root, never values; clipboard and secret-typed inputs carry no fingerprint), porting agent-native@9c277b79cb87eb27da538e572dd710986e2fa06d packages/core/src/agent/tool-call-journal.ts with its MIT notice and provenance recorded per AGENT_RUNTIME_INTEGRATION.md and the donor registry. Expose one read-only MCP tool task_resume_summary {task_id} -> {completed[], unknown[], next_verification[]} that forwards to a read-only orceld kernel operation (orcel-mcp never reads journal files itself), with remote: "local_only" in tool_contract.ts, listed only in the local profiles and proved by an exact profile-membership check; adding it to core, the remote ceiling, is outside this grain and needs its own decision. Another session's or workspace's task is refused.
exclude: Workspace trust grant and revoke (checksum-chained trust.jsonl), remote lease create and revoke (atomic checksummed lease store) and policy.change (refused at dispatch), which keep their existing records; and live-browser actions other than the SG-000108 download, which keep their existing confinement.
Any automatic retry or re-dispatch of a mutation whose outcome is unknown.
Any new mutation, approval class, approval reuse or approval carried in a journal entry or tool result.
Remote exposure of task_resume_summary or of any journal content (core profile, tunnel, relay, public edge).
Secret values, file contents or clipboard contents in journal entries (paths, sizes, hashes, states and outcomes only).
SG-000096 shell and process authority (it stays unarmed; RJ-02 journals process_spawn only as it exists today).
SG-000127 decisions (stop, takeover, signing, live browser in release builds).

authority_delta.activation: None. This packet authorizes implementing and proving SG-000120; it adds no capability, tool, dependency, listener or authority.
authority_delta.mcp: Proposed only (RJ-03): one local-only read-only tool, task_resume_summary; existing tools, schemas and the core membership unchanged.
authority_delta.filesystem: Proposed only: orceld writes its own journal files under its private state root; no user-visible file authority changes.
authority_delta.approval: Unchanged rules. Proposed only: an unknown outcome requires a new explicit approval before a dependent step; nothing is retried on a spent approval.
authority_delta.privileged: None. SG-000096 Full User shell remains unarmed.

decisions.question: Sequencing
decisions.decision: The founder, in the implementing session's chat on 2026-10-25 and recorded on tracking issue #455: "Founder sequencing: open SG-000120 (RJ-01 to RJ-03, durable journal and recovery) as an additional active grain alongside SG-000096 and SG-000127, with the canonical tests updated to record it." SG-000120 is activated on main f9d21e3af84f27c97fa460e236122bcf2a05377f and runs with SG-000096 and SG-000127 as the three open grains. Its proposed authority (journal files under orceld's state root, reconciliation that only reduces duplicate effects, one local read-only tool) is disjoint from both.

decisions.question: Donor reuse
decisions.decision: RJ-01 and RJ-02 are BUILD_NEW from Orcel's own qualified SG-000108 journal; SPACE (space@09e922efd23b3c0d109ab64de7e567a901bcc61e docs/architecture.md) is adopted only as rules (unknown process-start outcome, execution-generation fencing). RJ-03 PORTs agent-native's tool-call journal classification with provenance recorded per the donor registry.

decisions.question: Remote resume summary
decisions.decision: The backlog card proposed task_resume_summary in local and core profiles. This grain keeps it local_only; exposing it to remote clients needs its own decision and review.

invariants: orceld remains the sole local authority; the journal records what orceld decided and did, it never authorizes.
No retry: no dispatch happens under the same intent id or approval digest as a step whose outcome is unknown; re-running it needs a fresh approval and a fresh intent.
Journal entries hold paths, sizes, hashes, states and outcomes, never secret values, file contents or clipboard contents.
One writer per journal; a second writer is refused; a torn line is skipped with a typed warning and every other unreadable line fails closed, exactly as in SG-000108.
Existing MCP tool names, schemas, the core membership and the orcel-relay/1 frames are unchanged; the one new tool is local-only.
acceptance: RJ-01: crates/orcel-journal holds the journal; intents.jsonl is byte-compatible and the download writer emits only its four existing events; every SG-000108 suite passes unchanged; a second writer is refused; a torn line is skipped with a typed warning and any other unreadable line fails closed; a crash between pending and dispatch is listed by recover; the release-blocker sweep passes.

RJ-02: a fault-injection suite kills orceld at each transition for each mutating provider; after restart every interrupted step is reconciled as settled, abandoned or unknown and none is re-dispatched.
RJ-02: an fs or report mutation whose destination matches the approved digest reconciles as settled; a desktop action interrupted after dispatch is unknown and requires re-observation.
RJ-02: a dependent step after an unknown outcome is refused until a new explicit approval.
RJ-02: SG-000126 report tasks survive an orceld restart in task.list and task.get, and an approved commit interrupted before its reply is reconciled, not written twice.
RJ-02: the F2 report journey runs end to end with an induced crash after approval and before the reply; after restart the commit is reconciled against the destination and nothing is written twice.
RJ-03: task_resume_summary returns completed, unknown and next-verification entries after an induced crash, with hashed fingerprints only, and refuses another session's or workspace's task.
RJ-03: task_resume_summary is local_only, listed in the local profiles only, and core, the tunnel and the public edge neither list nor serve it.
RJ-03: an MCP client transcript shows a reconnecting local client reading the resume summary of an interrupted task.
Windows, macOS and Linux CI legs pass on each exact head.

review.alibaba_open_code_review: delegation mode per standing founder decision (2026-10-10) with manual review of excluded files
review.security_review: fresh-context security judge on RJ-01, RJ-02, RJ-03 and closeout; d1-local advisory only

successor_requirements.br_07: BR-07's independent browser postcondition verifier builds on the RJ-01 journal.
successor_requirements.remote_resume: A remote resume summary needs its own decision on the core profile and the remote threat model.

activation_note: No capability, tool, dependency or authority change in this activation packet. Separate implementation and closeout PRs must qualify their exact heads; activation CI alone proves nothing about the journal.

open_follow_ups: Remote resume summary (decision outside this grain, recorded in the spec).
Journal executable-registry upserts and browser download and upload effects if their scope widens (outside RJ-02's provider list).
BR-07's independent browser postcondition verifier builds on the RJ-01 journal.
Compact intents.jsonl (SG-000108 download intents) before the 16 MiB bound.
Surface torn journal lines (Lines::torn) beyond a stderr warning.
known_residuals: Dependent-step keys are the workspace and the normalized target only: an fs.move destination, paths under a directory made with --parents, and a UIA window against its element ids are not keyed as dependents; Windows trailing dots, 8.3 names, stream suffixes and links are not folded.
The unknown-target map is rebuilt from the newest 256 journal outcomes and is per orceld process.
A step that fails after its approval is consumed but before its effect starts is labelled unknown rather than abandoned (a label only; nothing is retried).
Reconciliation reads the target at start and can be raced by a writer between the check and the hash (a label only).

The MCP-level crash transcript (installed release, Windows) reads an interrupted task with no unknown commit: an approved commit cannot be driven through the real binaries without a person at the prompt; the unknown-commit summary is proven with a really aborted child process at unit level.

task_resume_summary serves the session that started the task; a restarted MCP client process or a new loopback session is a new session. The verification text names the destination path and the approved SHA-256.
Process, clipboard and desktop effects are journaled with the opaque postcondition and are never probed: an interrupted one is always unknown and needs re-observation.

Git provider hardening (#461): files tracked through a filter (Git LFS) can show as modified in git.status and git.diff; submodule changes are no longer reported by git.status or git.diff; the configuration is read in a separate process just before each command, so a driver added in that window is not seen.
Git journaling (#460): git.stage and git.unstage are not probed and git.push and git.fetch always reconcile as unknown; a starting orceld probes for at most 60 s and records the rest unknown.

File journaling (#459): targets written with '.' components reconcile as unknown; an mkdir --parents crash after a parent was deleted during the prompt can be labelled nothing_done although a parent was created.
Report journal (#458): on Linux, orcelds in different PID namespaces sharing one state root can judge each other exited.
RJ-01 (#457): intents.jsonl is never compacted and new downloads are refused near 16 MiB.

Process, clipboard and desktop wrappers (#462, #463) are tested through the shared journaled path, not end to end on a desktop; no test goes through the product dispatch_with for the unknown-outcome notice.
Resume summary (#464): preview and commit fingerprints use the task's current proposal; report-tasks.key is read without its own link or DACL check, relying on the owner-only state root.

done_when: On Windows, macOS and Linux, every mutating dispatch of the RJ-02 providers is journaled and reconciled after a crash without re-dispatch, report tasks survive a restart, and a reconnecting local client can read a bounded resume summary, with the fault-injection suite and exact-head CI passing.
